questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Last summer, the small town of Beni Khalled organised a clean-air week. The town council banned cars from the centre, and people went to work by bike. By Friday, the streets were quieter and the sky looked clearer. A doctor said on the local radio: 'I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week.' The mayor promised to repeat the event every year."

What can we infer from the doctor's words?

options.text: The doctor wanted the town to stop the event at once.
The hospital closed during the clean-air week.
Most people in the town were ill.
Cleaner air seemed to improve people's breathing.

questions.explanation: The clues are fewer patients with breathing problems during a week with fewer cars and a clearer sky: cleaner air seems to have helped people breathe. The doctor's positive report contradicts the idea that he wanted the event to stop, and a closed hospital or a town of ill people has no clue in the text — it is invented.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Last summer, the small town of Beni Khalled organised a clean-air week. The town council banned cars from the centre, and people went to work by bike. By Friday, the streets were quieter and the sky looked clearer. A doctor said on the local radio: 'I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week.' The mayor promised to repeat the event every year."

In the text, the word "banned" most probably means:

options.text: not allowed
allowed everywhere
repaired
sold cheaply

questions.explanation: The clue is what happened next: cars could not enter the centre, so people went to work by bike — "banned" means not allowed. "allowed everywhere" is the opposite, and repairing cars or selling them cheaply would not make people cycle to work.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Last summer, the small town of Beni Khalled organised a clean-air week. The town council banned cars from the centre, and people went to work by bike. By Friday, the streets were quieter and the sky looked clearer. A doctor said on the local radio: 'I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week.' The mayor promised to repeat the event every year."

Language: complete this sentence about the text:

"People went to work by bike ______ the council banned cars from the centre."

options.text: so
therefore
because
whereas

questions.explanation: The part after the gap — the council banned cars — is the cause of cycling, and a cause is introduced by "because". "so" and "therefore" introduce a result, but banning cars is not a result of cycling, and "whereas" needs two opposite ideas.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Last summer, the small town of Beni Khalled organised a clean-air week. The town council banned cars from the centre, and people went to work by bike. By Friday, the streets were quieter and the sky looked clearer. A doctor said on the local radio: 'I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week.' The mayor promised to repeat the event every year."

Language: the doctor says "I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week". Why does he use the present perfect?

options.text: He talks about a finished time in the past.
He gives news about a recent change.
He describes an action in progress in the past.
He announces a plan for next week.

questions.explanation: The present perfect gives news and describes a change between the past and now, and "this week" is not finished yet. A finished time such as "last week" would take the simple past, an action in progress in the past takes the past progressive (was/were + verb-ing), and a plan for next week needs a future form.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Last summer, the small town of Beni Khalled organised a clean-air week. The town council banned cars from the centre, and people went to work by bike. By Friday, the streets were quieter and the sky looked clearer. A doctor said on the local radio: 'I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week.' The mayor promised to repeat the event every year."

Language: complete this sentence about the text:

"If more towns ______ cars from their centres, the air will be cleaner."

options.text: will ban
banned
are banning
ban

questions.explanation: This is the first conditional: if + present simple, then will + verb in the result. The result already has "will be", so the if-clause takes the present simple: "If more towns ban cars…". "will ban" puts will after if, "banned" is the simple past, and "are banning" describes an action in progress, not a condition.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

"Last summer, the small town of Beni Khalled organised a clean-air week. The town council banned cars from the centre, and people went to work by bike. By Friday, the streets were quieter and the sky looked clearer. A doctor said on the local radio: 'I have seen fewer patients with breathing problems this week.' The mayor promised to repeat the event every year."

Writing: which sentence would be the best topic sentence for a paragraph summarising this text?

options.text: A clean-air week made Beni Khalled healthier.
The mayor spoke on the local radio on Friday.
Some people prefer cars to bikes in the summer.
As a result, the sky looked clearer by Friday.

questions.explanation: A topic sentence is general and announces the whole idea: a clean-air week that made the town healthier. The words on the radio were the doctor's, not the mayor's, so that sentence is also a false detail; preferring cars is off the topic; and a sentence opening with "As a result" gives one result, so it cannot open the paragraph.
